fixes.row: Judging the living and the dead, the world, the nations
fixes.why: The label says 'the living and the dead', a phrase these verses do not use. Isa 2:4 says He will judge between the nations and Ps 96:13 says He is coming to judge the earth. Filing Hebrew Scripture under a New Testament last-judgment heading is the framing the hub's own rule 5 forbids, and it misstates the label's own rule 1.
fixes.fix: Relabel to 'Judging the earth, the peoples and the nations; judging the living and the dead', and keep the words 'the living and the dead' for the verses that say them (2 Tim 4:1; Acts 10:42; 1 Pet 4:5-6).

fixes.row: Told not to judge, and rebuked for judging
fixes.why: James 5:9 reads in the Berean: 'Do not complain about one another, brothers, so that you will not be judged. Look, the Judge is standing at the door!' It rebukes grumbling, not judging, so the row's label does not say what this verse says. It already stands in the row 'A judge, the Judge'.
fixes.fix: Remove Jas 5:9 from 'Told not to judge, and rebuked for judging'. It stays in 'A judge, the Judge; all judgment to the Son'.

fixes.row: Judgment and the world, the nations
fixes.why: The first example is Matt 12:18, the New Testament quoting Isa 42:1 in an Old Testament row. The row's note is null, yet who the Servant of Isa 42:1 is stands as a contested reading (Israel, or the Messiah), and the page says nothing about it. The rabbi would see the Christian application presented as the verse's own sense.
fixes.fix: Lead the examples with Isa 42:1 (Berean: 'Here is My Servant ... He will bring justice to the nations') instead of Matt 12:18. Add a note: 'Who the Servant of Isa 42:1 is, readers take differently; the page does not choose.'

fixes.row: Judged, and works, deeds, ways + Judged, and believing, faith
fixes.why: In the verb form the works row stands first and the believing row second, and each note only says 'set beside the next/previous row'. Read down the page, works comes before faith, which settles an order the rule 2 forbids. Both notes say the page takes no side, but the placement does.
fixes.fix: Merge the two rows into one, 'Judged by works, ways and deeds, and by believing: according to each one's work; whoever believes in Him is not condemned' (21 verses, 15 plus 6, with the notes combined). The row count falls to 25 and no order is left to read.

fixes.row: The day of judgment, the hour of judgment; “at the judgment”; “after that to face judgment”; the judgment seat of God; the court seated, the books opened
fixes.why: Ps 1:5 in the Berean: 'Therefore the wicked will not stand in the judgment, nor sinners in the assembly of the righteous.' It is an Old Testament sentence about standing in a court's judgment, filed under the New Testament heading for a day of judgment. The label's 'at the judgment' is quoted from it, so the row is shaped by a verse that is not an eschatological day.
fixes.fix: Move Ps 1:5 to 'In the gate and the court: judges, elders, witnesses, bribes; trials and sentences', where standing in judgment belongs.

fixes.why: The hub's own spec drops about 163 verses where מִשְׁפָּט is 'statute', 'ordinance' or 'custom' (Deut 4:5 in the Berean: 'I have taught you statutes and ordinances'). They appear in no row and the page does not say so, so the word is presented as judgment throughout. That breaks rule 4 (one sense is never the whole). The Torah's central legal word is read as only its court sense on the page.
fixes.fix: Add to this row's note: 'About 163 verses where mishpat means statute, ordinance or custom (for example Deut 4:5 and Lev 18:4) are not shown here. They are another sense of the word.' Do not add the verses to the judgment rows.

worker_points.point: The final judgment and what follows: the hub is silent on annihilationist and universalist proof-texts with no judgment word (Matt 10:28, Rom 11:32, 1 Cor 15:22, Col 1:20).
worker_points.why: The limit is stated in the report. Scope is for Doug to decide, and it is listed under missing.

worker_points.point: Judgment by works beside being counted righteous by faith; believing row small (6).
worker_points.why: The order of the two verb rows tilts the page; merge them (fix 4).

worker_points.point: God's justice in Israel's courts kept as its own sense; Isa 53:8 and Acts 8:33 in the courts row with no reading of who is meant.
worker_points.why: The text's sense is kept apart and the Isa 53 row is neutral as written.

worker_points.point: Divine persons by hand: God, Jesus, 'the Lord, He, the One'; Jesus verses side by side.
worker_points.why: By hand, with a note that the page does not choose.

worker_points.point: 'Do not judge' and 'judge righteously' in adjacent rows.
worker_points.why: The adjacency is acceptable with the note. The misfit is Jas 5:9 only (fix 2).

worker_points.point: Isa 11:3-4 in the judges row, with a note that readers differ on whom it means.
worker_points.why: The note keeps the reading open.

worker_points.point: Mark 16:16 (longer ending) flagged in the believing and condemn rows.
Hard verses kept: Rev 20:12-13, 1 Pet 4:6, Job and prophets' complaints beside Job 34:12.
Placement of Rom 2:5 and 2 Thess 1:5 in the LORD's justice row; Ezek 21:27 under every other use.
worker_points.why: Each placement follows what the verse says of the judgment.

missing.what: The sheep and the goats (Matt 25:31-46), the judgment scene the gather list names, is in no row because the verses have no judgment word. A biblical-theological reader will look for it on this page. Doug must decide whether the scope rule (judgment word only) is kept here or a by-hand row is added.

1 Cor 3:15 in the Berean: 'If it is burned up, he will suffer loss ... saved, but only as if through the flames.' It is the Day testing each work by fire, with no judgment word. Catholic and Eastern Orthodox readers take it as part of what follows judgment, and the 'fire' row omits it.

The faith side of the works and faith question is six verses in the believing row. Rom 4:5 (faith credited as righteousness to the one who does not work) has no judgment word and so is absent, although Lutheran and Reformed readers will expect it beside the works verses.

examples_checked: 25 of 26 rows: all four examples show their label. The exception is 'Judging the living and the dead, the world, the nations': 2 of its 4 examples (Ps 96:13, Joel 3:12) say judge the earth or nations but not 'the living and the dead'.
summary: The hub is faithful to the text in its rows and notes, and it keeps the contested points visibly open. It needs six fixes before it can ship: a label that names the living and the dead over Old Testament verses, a James 5:9 misfit, an Isaiah 42 row that leads with a New Testament quotation and states no note on the Servant, a verb order that tilts works before faith, one Old Testament verse under a day-of-judgment heading, and an undisclosed exclusion of the ordinance sense of mishpat.
